# NN. The stage's name

**Where you are.** One or two sentences: what the student has now, and
what they do not have yet.

**The question.** One open question about the student's own app, on a
line by itself, that this stage helps them answer.

A real moment from one of my apps, quoted from the prompt or the commit
that shows it, with its date. It shows the stage's idea happening, and it
can be messy. (On the novice path, this is the worked example the steps
lean on.)

**The stage in one line, in bold.**

## The idea, in a few short sections

Only what a novice needs to understand before they start. Each section
answers one thing they will wonder.

## Working with your agent

The steps are one round of write, play, publish. Step 1 and step 2 come
before the agent is open, the middle steps are play, with the agent and
on your device, and the last step publishes to a person.

1. **Write your first answer.** Before any prompt, answer the question at
   the top of this stage in two or three sentences in your note. Being
   wrong is fine. You will come back to it.

2. **Write your questions.** For five minutes, write as many questions
   as you can about the question at the top, without stopping to answer
   or judge any of them. Then mark the one you most want answered by the
   end of this stage.

3. **Play: the first conversation.** What to say to the agent, as a
   prompt the student adapts, with one of mine quoted as the worked
   example. If this is your first app, read mine first. If it is not,
   write yours first and read mine after.

   > A real prompt of mine, quoted exactly.

4. **Play: look on the device.** Open the app where its people will use
   it, use it for real, and write down what you saw, numbered, in your
   note. Then send it to the agent as one round.

5. **Publish: one decision, with the agent closed.** In two sentences in
   your note: one thing you decided in this stage, and what it cost. Then
   show the work to one person, and write down what they did first.

Where the agents differ, one line each, never more:

- **Claude Code:** the one thing that is different there.
- **Antigravity:** the one thing that is different there.
- **The open path:** the one thing that is different there.

**When you are ready to move on,** the things that must be true of the
student's own app, each one something a partner can see on a device.
Ready, or not yet: the student judges first.

**Go deeper.** One extension for someone who wants more. It is never
required, and it is never counted.

**If you get stuck.** The stuck moments this stage most often makes, each
as a question to ask yourself first, then what to try, then who to ask.

**Before you close your note.** Four short lines, from my
[Educational Model Spec's AI Disclosure Protocol](https://github.com/bhwilkoff/educational-model-spec/blob/main/docs/implementation-tools/ai_disclosure_protocol.md):
the agent's role, your essential work, one thing you learned, and your
growth edge.

Be ready to show something specific on a device, and to explain one
decision behind it in your own words, with the agent closed.
